ai.description: This slender snake reaches 80–100 cm. It is pale brown with two rows of dark, rounded blotches along the back and a distinct V-shaped mark on the head. It features a pointed snout and vertical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga multomaculata* is best distinguished by the two distinct, dark longitudinal stripes running from the nape onto the back of the head, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Many-spotted Cat Snake inhabits lowland tropical forests, bamboo thickets, and scrublands, typically found at elevations below 1,000 meters in the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Many-spotted Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal and arboreal, often hunting small lizards and birds by stealthily stalking them among the branches.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga multomaculata* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding in India generally occurs during the warmer, pre-monsoon months.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Boiga multomaculata* is found in Northeast India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh) and the Eastern Himalayas, typically inhabiting low-to-mid elevation tropical forests.
